attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The branch has no concrete carrier that is simultaneously a weak same-model source lower bound and target-preserving. Same-model sources demagnify; restricted sources need an unproved substitution-closure theorem.
steps: Start from the repaired cycle-8 interface: reduction overhead exponent a, query-count exponent q, and SAT query length L(N)=N^{o(1)} with max(a,q)<1+epsilon.
Inline a hypothetical size-L^c SAT circuit into every SAT oracle gate of the carrier reduction, obtaining C(K_N)<=s_R(N)+Q(N)L(N)^c+O(Q(N)L(N)).
Observe that this proves the valid target transfer: an eventual N^{1+epsilon} lower bound for K_N excludes every fixed c because L(N)^c=N^{o(1)}.
Read the same inequality contrapositively: the source lower bound implies C(SAT_{<=L(N)})>(N^{1+epsilon}-s_R-O(QL))/Q.
For Q<=N^q with q<1+epsilon and L=N^{o(1)}, the induced SAT lower bound is N^{1+epsilon-q-o(1)}=L^{omega(1)}, already superpolynomial at the target query length.
Add the unconditional lookup upper bound C(K_N)<=s_R+O(QL2^L), yielding a lower-edge falsifier L >= (1+epsilon-q-o(1))log_2 N for any possible N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This certifies failure of the black-box subpolynomial SAT-interface route, not P != NP. It does not rule out nonblackbox carriers, proof-complexity carriers, derandomization objects, or lower bounds in models with a valid independent closure theorem.

assumptions: Circuit model is nonuniform Boolean SIZE with ordinary closure under composition.
All query strings have length at most L(N), and the SAT circuit substituted is a single circuit family correct on all valid encodings up to that length.
Q(N)>=1 and L(N) is unbounded on infinitely many N when deriving a P/poly separation consequence.
The source lower bound is against the same general circuit model, not a weaker class such as AC0 or bounded-depth formulas.
definitions: source object: an explicit Boolean family K_N on N input bits with a DLOGTIME-uniform reduction circuit R_N of size s_R(N), making Q(N) oracle calls to SAT instances of length at most L(N).

target object: SAT restricted to encodings of length at most L(N), measured in nonuniform SIZE; if lower bounds hold for unbounded L(N), the target consequence is SAT notin P/poly, hence NP not subset P/poly.
controlled interface: substitute a size-T circuit for each SAT query in R_N, preserving query count Q(N), reduction overhead s_R(N), and postprocessing fan-in without hidden advice.

target-preserving condition: the reduction family is uniform or explicitly constructible, L(N)=N^{o(1)}, s_R(N)<N^{1+epsilon}, Q(N)<N^{1+epsilon}, and the same SIZE model is used on source and target.

equations.label: upper_transfer
equations.valid_when: Applies when every oracle answer is replaced by a target SAT circuit and the reduction overhead is counted explicitly.

equations.label: contrapositive_demagnification
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source lower bound exceeds the complete substituted reduction size threshold in the same circuit model.

equations.label: subpoly_query_consequence
equations.latex: L(N)=N^{o(1)},\ Q(N)\le N^q,\ s_R(N)\le N^a,\ a,q<1+\epsilon \Rightarrow C_{\mathrm{SIZE}}(\mathrm{SAT}_{\le L(N)})\ge N^{1+\epsilon-q-o(1)}=L(N)^{\omega(1)}
equations.valid_when: Requires the subpolynomial query-length regime and polynomially bounded query count below the claimed source threshold.

equations.label: lookup_falsifier_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source model is unrestricted nonuniform circuits and lookup tables may encode SAT truth tables.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier fires if L(N)2^{L(N)}Q(N)=o(N^{1+epsilon}) because lookup circuits kill the source lower bound; another fires if the intended proof is advertised as barely nontrivial while equation contrapositive_demagnification forces SAT_{<=L} lower bounds of size L^{omega(1)}.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route refutation plus calibrated bridge: the same inequality that transfers SAT upper bounds to K_N lower-bound consequences shows that same-model subpolynomial-query magnification smuggles a superpolynomial SAT lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a carrier K_N decided by a near-linear circuit reduction making Q(N) SAT queries of length L(N)=N^{o(1)}, an N^{1+epsilon} lower bound in the same nonuniform SIZE model is not a weak magnification source. Read contrapositively, it already implies a superpolynomial lower bound for SAT at the query length. The bridge is valid as a target transfer but fails as a same-model weak-source route.

assumptions: M must be closed under the reduction and under oracle-answer substitution with the stated size bound.
The transfer cannot use nonuniform advice depending on K_N beyond the named reduction R_N.
Restricted-source lower bounds are counted in M-size, while target upper bounds are counted in general circuit size.
definitions: source model M: the class against which K_N is lower bounded, such as SIZE, formulas, AC0, AC0[p], or another explicitly named circuit family.
target model: general nonuniform circuits for SAT, usually SAT in SIZE(n^c) for a fixed c or SAT in P/poly.
interface closure: a quantitative substitution map Phi_M converting R_N plus Q SAT circuits of size T into an M-circuit for K_N.
model-mismatch obstruction: SAT in SIZE(L^c) alone gives no AC0, formula-depth, monotone, or algebraic-depth simulation unless Phi_M is separately proved.

equations.label: restricted_transfer_obligation
equations.valid_when: Applies only after a real closure lemma for the named restricted model M is established.

equations.label: general_size_special_case
equations.valid_when: Valid for ordinary nonuniform circuits because arbitrary substituted circuits compose without depth or gate-type restrictions.

equations.label: model_mismatch_failure
equations.valid_when: Requires a restricted source model where substitution of general SAT circuits may violate the source-model syntax.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If M=SIZE, the route is demagnified by L1; if M is restricted and Phi_M is missing or exceeds N^{1+epsilon}, the bridge is invalid by model mismatch rather than by P vs NP folklore.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier audit: separates a quantitative same-model falsifier from a model-preservation gap for weaker source models.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A subpolynomial SAT-interface route has a dichotomy. If the source lower-bound model is general SIZE, Lemma L1 demagnifies the source into a superpolynomial SAT lower bound. If the source model is restricted, the target-preserving transfer is valid only after proving a closure theorem showing that substituting arbitrary small SAT circuits keeps the carrier inside the restricted source model below the threshold.

control_decision.pivot_test: Continue this route only if a named restricted source model M and an explicit Phi_M substitution bound below N^{1+epsilon} are supplied without assuming the target separation.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only a carrier whose lower-bound model, transfer closure, and thresholds avoid both the L^{omega(1)} SAT demagnification and the lookup-table falsifier.
control_decision.reason: The route is target-preserving but not weak-source magnification: its source lower bound is quantitatively at least a superpolynomial SAT lower bound at the compressed query length.

dependency_updates.description: The subpolynomial-query bridge is a valid implication but not a same-model hardness magnification theorem; contraposition forces superpolynomial SAT lower bounds at query length.
If the source model is SIZE, the route demagnifies. If the source model is restricted, the missing dependency is an explicit closure bound Phi_M under substitution of general SAT circuits.
The NP not subset P/poly consequence is valid only when L(N) is unbounded on infinitely many source lengths and the reduction is uniform enough to avoid advice leakage.

The present obstruction is quantitative and model-theoretic, not merely natural-proofs folklore. Any surviving carrier must be nonblackbox, nonrelativizing, or in a source model with a genuine target-preserving closure theorem.

falsifiers: same-model demagnification falsifier: an N^{1+epsilon} lower bound for K_N entails SAT_{<=L(N)} lower bounds of size L(N)^{omega(1)}, so the source is not barely nontrivial relative to the target.
lookup-table falsifier: if Q(N)L(N)2^{L(N)}=o(N^{1+epsilon}) after reduction overhead, unrestricted nonuniform circuits decide K_N below the claimed threshold.
model-mismatch falsifier: replacing the source model by AC0, formulas, or another restricted class invalidates the transfer unless a quantitative substitution-closure lemma Phi_M is proved.
nonuniform leakage falsifier: if R_N or the compressor is chosen with advice encoding a hard truth table, the carrier lower bound is not target-preserving.

relativizing-interface falsifier: a proof using only black-box oracle substitution remains within a relativizing interface and cannot by itself overcome the known oracle barrier for the main P vs NP conjecture.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 9 converts the cycle-8 repair into a route failure certificate. Subpolynomial SAT queries remove the c-dependent upper-bound term, but the same transfer read backward says that proving the source N^{1+epsilon} lower bound in general SIZE already proves SAT_{<=L} has L^{omega(1)} circuits lower bounds. The remaining valid work is not carrier search inside this black-box same-model interface; it is either a restricted-model closure theorem or a nonblackbox carrier.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Pivot to a nonblackbox object: test a proof-complexity or derandomization carrier where SAT in P/poly yields the required source upper bound through a named nonrelativizing theorem rather than through black-box SAT-query substitution.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The route needs lower bound exponents k exceeding (1+beta)d for every desired SAT exponent d, but a fixed barely-nontrivial MCSP lower bound supplies only one eroded exponent window.
steps: Instantiate L with MCSP_s on truth-table length N and threshold s=N^beta; MCSP_s is in NP via guessing an s-size circuit and checking all N truth-table positions.
Compile the verifier and Cook-Levin reduction to get m(N)=~O(Ns)=N^{1+beta+o(1)} and reduction circuits of comparable size.
Assume a source lower bound MCSP_s notin SIZE(N^k). If SAT has m^d-size circuits, composition gives MCSP_s circuits of size N^{max{1+beta,(1+beta)d}+o(1)}.
Contradiction occurs only when k>max{1+beta,(1+beta)d}. For d>=1 this is d<k/(1+beta)-o(1).
For s=polylog N and k=1+epsilon, the valid conclusion is only SAT notin SIZE(m^{1+epsilon-o(1)}). This is not P != NP and not SAT notin P/poly.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation is a valid route lemma, not a lower-bound proof. It does not prove MCSP_s lower bounds and it does not escape natural-proof, relativization, or algebrization barriers for the source theorem.

assumptions: The source lower bound is worst-case and nonuniform on infinitely many or all relevant lengths, matching the target quantifier.
The reduction is length-regular enough that SAT circuits for lengths up to m(N) can be selected without advice depending on the input x.
Polylogarithmic factors are absorbed by a positive exponent slack eta>0.
No claim is made that the source lower-bound proof itself avoids relativization, natural proofs, or algebrization.
definitions: source object: L_N in NP, instantiated by MCSP_s on input length N with threshold s<=N^beta and a claimed lower bound L_N notin SIZE(N^k).
target object: SAT_m as the NP-complete target language, measured against nonuniform Boolean circuits of size m^d.
controlled interface: a uniform many-one reduction R_N from L_N to SAT with output length m(N)<=N^lambda polylog N and nonuniform circuit complexity |R_N|<=N^rho polylog N.
target-preserving condition: max{rho,lambda d}<k, so a target circuit for SAT composes with R_N without exceeding the forbidden source size.

equations.label: composition_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when the reduction is length-regular and compilable into nonuniform circuits with the stated exponent bounds.

equations.label: transfer_threshold
equations.latex: \text{SAT}\notin \operatorname{SIZE}(m^d)\quad\text{for every }d\text{ with }\exists\eta>0:\rho\le k-\eta\text{ and }\lambda d\le k-\eta.
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source lower bound excludes N^k-size circuits with enough slack to absorb lower-order factors.

equations.label: mcsp_cook_parameters
equations.valid_when: Applies when MCSP verification enumerates all truth-table positions and Cook-Levin is near-linear up to logarithmic factors.

equations.label: mcsp_to_sat_exponent
equations.valid_when: Requires the MCSP verifier size and output length to dominate no more than N to the one plus beta.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any proposed magnification step deriving SAT notin P/poly from one fixed k without an exponent amplifier or a family of source lower bounds k(d)>lambda d.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route-level quantitative bridge and threshold-collapse audit for MCSP/NP-source lower bounds transferred to SAT.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If an NP source language L on length N has a nonuniform lower bound L_N notin SIZE(N^k) and reduces to SAT by a length-N^lambda, circuit-N^rho many-one map, then SAT_m notin SIZE(m^d) only for exponents with max{rho,lambda d}<k. Thus a fixed barely-nontrivial source lower bound transfers only to a fixed eroded SAT lower bound, not to P != NP.

assumptions: The target is nonuniform SAT lower bounds, stronger than P != NP but a standard route certificate.
The bridge uses only composition and does not create new hardness.
BGS-style oracle collapse remains a falsifier for any fully relativizing attempt to prove the required source lower bounds uniformly over all oracles.
definitions: fixed-exponent source lower bound: exclusion of circuits of size N^k for one constant k.
P-vs-NP target requirement: exclusion of m^d-size SAT circuits for every constant d, or equivalently SAT notin P/poly as a nonuniform strengthening.
exponent amplifier: an additional theorem converting one fixed k into an unbounded family of target exponents without advice leakage.
barrier status: the transfer lemma relativizes, so the lower-bound source or amplifier must provide the nonrelativizing/non-natural/non-algebrizing content.

equations.label: pnp_requirement
equations.valid_when: Valid when SAT is measured as a nonuniform language family over standard Boolean circuits.

equations.label: unbounded_exponent_obligation
equations.latex: \forall d\; k(d)>\max\{\rho,\lambda d\}\quad\text{is needed for Karp-transfer proof of }\mathrm{SAT}\notin\mathrm{P/poly}.
equations.valid_when: Requires ordinary many-one transfer with no separate padding theorem or hardness amplification mechanism.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the claimed route has only k=1+epsilon and lambda>=1, then SAT circuits of exponent 2 are a formal falsifier to the claimed implication.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quarantines invalid extrapolation from weak lower bounds to the main conjecture while preserving the useful finite-exponent transfer.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A single lower bound L_N notin SIZE(N^k) for an NP-complete or NP source language, even when valid and non-natural, cannot by ordinary Karp transfer imply P != NP; it can rule out only target circuit exponents below the eroded threshold.

control_decision.pivot_test: Quarantine any next proposal that gives only one fixed exponent k and asserts P != NP without naming lambda, rho, and an exponent amplifier.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if the route supplies either a family k(d)>lambda d for all d or a nonrelativizing, non-natural, non-algebrizing amplifier with no advice leakage.
control_decision.reason: The branch obtained a concrete quantitative transfer and a precise threshold collapse; the main conjecture remains untouched because unbounded target exponents are not produced.

dependency_updates.description: Karp transfer loses exponent by the reduction length lambda and reduction circuit cost rho; fixed-k lower bounds cannot become P-vs-NP certificates.
The bridge is not a natural property, but any constructive large proof of the MCSP source lower bound remains subject to the natural-proofs falsifier.
The composition bridge relativizes; this is harmless for finite-exponent transfer but insufficient for proving the unbounded lower-bound family required for SAT notin P/poly.
Nonuniform SAT circuits compose with a fixed reduction without extra input-dependent advice; the cost is already charged as rho and lambda.

falsifiers: Concrete falsifier: MCSP_s notin SIZE(N^1.1) together with SAT in SIZE(m^2) violates no displayed inequality when lambda is about 1.
Concrete falsifier: if the Cook-Levin or verifier interface has lambda>=k, no nontrivial d>=1 SAT lower bound transfers.
Concrete falsifier: if the source lower bound is only average-case with advantage N^{-a}, the worst-case SAT lower bound is invalid without a separate worst-case-to-average-case bridge.
Concrete falsifier: if the MCSP lower-bound proof is poly(N)-constructive, large, and useful against SIZE(N^k), the natural-proof audit from cycle 1 applies under standard PRF assumptions.
Concrete falsifier: a fully relativizing proof of the unbounded source lower-bound family would be incompatible with oracle collapses where P^O=NP^O.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 9 turns weak-source-to-SAT enthusiasm into an explicit exponent accounting lemma. A lower bound N^k for MCSP_s with s=N^beta transfers through Cook-Levin only to SAT exponents d<k/(1+beta)-o(1). This is valid route-level progress and a falsifier for claims that one barely-superlinear source lower bound by itself implies P != NP.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The bridge is now valid only after adding a uniform expander/selector. The unsolved gap is constructing such a sparse sound certificate-expander without already proving the desired circuit lower bound by another route.
steps: Start with the previous certificate bridge and separate two notions: external verification V(T,pi) versus generated verification V(m,pi) for T=tt(G_{m,pi}).
For the generated model, enumerate all O(m)-bit pi and all m<=n to find the largest accepted source length M(n) and its lexicographically first certificate pi_M.
Define L on length n by padding down to the accepted hard slice: L(x)=G(M(n),pi_M,prefix_M(x)). The search and evaluation cost 2^{O(n)}, so L is in E.
If a size s circuit computes L_n, then fixing the last n-M(n) inputs gives a size s circuit for G_{M,pi_M}. Soundness gives s>2^{epsilon M(n)}.
Kappa-density gives M(n)>=n/kappa-O(1), hence for every fixed delta<epsilon/kappa and all large n, C_n(L_n)>2^{delta n}.
For the external model without G, the search over T ranges over 2^{2^m} truth tables and cannot be performed in E; thus the old formulation had a witness-location gap.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This gives a route-level implication to E lower bounds under a strong source object. It neither constructs the source object nor implies P != NP by itself.

assumptions: Constants epsilon>0, kappa>=1, c,d,q<infinity are fixed independently of m.
For every sufficiently large n there is an accepted source length m in [n/kappa-O(1), n].
Circuit size C_m(f) is measured for m-input Boolean circuits with a fixed finite gate basis.
The verifier's soundness is semantic: every accepted generated table is outside circuits of size 2^{epsilon m}.
definitions: source object: uniform certificate-expander pair (G,V) with |pi|<=c m, G(m,pi,i) outputting the i-th bit of an m-input truth table in 2^{q m} time, V(m,pi) running in 2^{d m} time, and soundness V(m,pi)=1 implies MCSP(tt(G_{m,pi}))>2^{epsilon m}.

target object: deterministic E language L_{G,V} whose n-bit slice pads the latest accepted source length m<=n and has Boolean circuit complexity at least 2^{delta n} for each fixed delta<epsilon/kappa.

controlled interface: choose the lexicographically first accepted pi_m by exhaustive uniform search, set m=M(n) to the largest accepted source length at most n, and compute L(x)=G(m,pi_m,prefix_m(x)) without advice.
target-preserving condition: accepted source lengths are kappa-dense, V is sound at threshold 2^{epsilon m}, G and V have 2^{O(m)} uniform algorithms, and no nonuniform selector chooses pi_m.

equations.label: source truth-table length
equations.valid_when: Valid when the MCSP object is the full truth table of an m-bit Boolean function.

equations.label: canonical accepted length
equations.valid_when: Applies after accepted source lengths are uniformly searchable and kappa-dense below every large n.

equations.label: canonical slice
equations.valid_when: Valid when pi_m is the lexicographically first accepted certificate found by uniform exhaustive search.

equations.label: E-time search bound
equations.valid_when: Requires certificate length O(m) and verifier and generator running times bounded by 2^{O(m)}.

equations.label: source soundness threshold
equations.valid_when: Requires the verifier soundness to certify high MCSP for the generated table, not for an external witness.

equations.label: all-length transfer
equations.valid_when: Applies after padding from the latest accepted source length preserves circuits by fixing unused inputs.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: if certificates only verify V(T,pi) for an externally supplied T and no uniform G or selector produces T, the bridge cannot construct an E language and is not valid.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Repairs the previous bridge by adding the missing witness-location interface and gives the exact quantitative exponent transfer delta<epsilon/kappa.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A certificate verifier over externally supplied truth tables is not enough. If the source is a uniform certificate-expander pair (G,V) whose accepted O(m)-bit certificates generate truth tables of MCSP greater than 2^{epsilon m} on kappa-dense source lengths, then exhaustive uniform search defines a language in E with all-length circuit lower bound 2^{delta n} for every fixed delta<epsilon/kappa. This is a valid route bridge, not a proof of P != NP.

assumptions: There is a constant a such that Pr_T[R_m(T)=1]>=N^{-a} on the relevant length set.
The PRF family has truth tables computable by circuits of size at most N^epsilon.
The distinguisher is allowed to read the whole N-bit truth table, so its running time is polynomial in N.
definitions: source object: external verifier V_m(T,pi) over N=2^m bit truth tables with |pi|<=c m, time N^d, and soundness V_m(T,pi)=1 implies C(T)>N^epsilon.
target object: P-time natural property R_m useful against circuits of size N^epsilon and a distinguisher for small-circuit PRF truth tables.
controlled interface: enumerate all O(m)-bit certificates to decide R_m(T)=exists pi V_m(T,pi) in polynomial time in N.
target-preserving condition: the density lower bound, soundness threshold, and PRF security parameter all refer to the same truth-table length N.

equations.label: natural property
equations.valid_when: Valid when the external certificate verifier is uniform and certificates have logarithmic length in N.

equations.label: constructivity
equations.valid_when: Applies because enumerating all certificates costs only polynomial time in the truth-table length.

equations.label: largeness
equations.valid_when: Requires an inverse-polynomial acceptance density, so sparse carrier families do not satisfy this premise.

equations.label: PRF distinguishing advantage
equations.valid_when: Valid when every PRF truth table has circuit complexity at most N^epsilon and R_m is sound.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: a proposed dense verifier contradicts standard PRF security assumptions unless it is nonconstructive, not useful, or below inverse-polynomial density.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quarantines dense external-certificate repairs by identifying the formal natural-proofs obstruction they create.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the repair is attempted by an external verifier whose existentially accepted truth-table property has density at least N^{-a}, then certificate enumeration makes a P-natural property useful against size N^epsilon circuits. Under PRFs of circuit size at most N^epsilon secure against poly(N)-time tests with advantage N^{-a}, this dense route is blocked. Sparse expander-generated sources remain outside this falsifier.

assumptions: epsilon>0 is constant.
Circuit descriptions of size S have O(S log S) bits under any standard encoding.
Comparing one candidate circuit to the truth table costs at least 2^m evaluations or table lookups.
definitions: source object: generated truth table f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} with claimed circuit lower bound S=2^{epsilon m}.
target object: 2^{O(m)}-time sound verifier usable inside the E extraction bridge.
controlled interface: verification may inspect the generated truth table but must not enumerate all circuits of size S.
target-preserving condition: soundness must remain at threshold S=2^{epsilon m} while verification stays exponential only in m.

equations.label: number of circuits
equations.valid_when: Valid for standard bounded fan-in circuit encodings with size S=2^{epsilon m}.

equations.label: bruteforce verification time
equations.valid_when: Applies when soundness is checked by comparing against every circuit below the claimed threshold.

equations.label: threshold collapse
equations.valid_when: Requires epsilon to be a fixed positive constant, making circuit enumeration super-exponential in m.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: if the certificate verifier secretly performs circuit enumeration at threshold 2^{epsilon m}, it violates the source time budget and invalidates the extraction theorem.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Shows that the remaining source problem is genuine and cannot be solved by an exhaustive MCSP verifier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The verifier in the selector-expander bridge cannot certify MCSP>N^epsilon by naive enumeration of all circuits. For S=2^{epsilon m}, brute-force lower-bound checking takes 2^{Theta(S log S)} times truth-table evaluation, which is far above 2^{O(m)}. Any valid source certificate must encode a nontrivial, non-natural, nonuniform-free proof of high MCSP.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if every candidate source either lacks a uniform expander, uses advice to select certificates, accepts an inverse-polynomial dense property, or verifies soundness by circuit enumeration.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if we exhibit a kappa-dense family of O(m)-bit certificates with generator G and verifier V running in 2^{O(m)} such that V soundly proves MCSP(tt(G_{m,pi}))>2^{epsilon m} without natural largeness or nonuniform leakage.
control_decision.reason: The route has a valid bridge after strengthening the interface, but the remaining progress must construct or refute the sparse expander certificate source rather than restate MCSP hardness folklore.

dependency_updates.description: The carrier must be generated by a uniform certificate-expander; an existential no-side truth table is not enough for extraction.
Kappa-dense generated high-MCSP certificates at threshold 2^{epsilon m} transfer to E circuit lower bounds 2^{delta n} for every delta<epsilon/kappa.
Explicitness now means E-time discovery of an accepted certificate and E-time bit evaluation of its generated hard truth table.
Dense external verifiers become P-natural useful properties and are conditionally blocked by PRF security; sparse expander images avoid largeness.
Need a non-natural, nonuniform-free, 2^{O(m)}-verifiable proof of MCSP>N^epsilon for generated tables; brute force is quantitatively invalid.
